Candidate sha256:d8d831814a6065af8b417c862486dc2132ee6cca40bae0573f4918ff52e782c9 (2203 files, source 54e02b61961550386d5ab24a74e8ae8bb612218f), recomputed in a complete disposable clone at the start and at the end of my run. The owner is frontend-ux-engineer (T-DG5-FE-RG2); I authored none of the repair. fix_revision 1d8d6d56a11279e92be044d51686a03e26e4b56e is a commit and an ancestor of 54e02b6 (03-findings-fix-ancestry.log). The diff edbf5ce..54e02b6 touches only two test files. In p3-prioritization-roadmap.spec.ts the substring matcher /approve|اعتماد|move|نقل/i is replaced by the whole-word APPROVE_OR_MOVE = /(?<![\p{L}\p{M}])(?:approve|move|اعتماد|نقل)(?![\p{L}\p{M}])/iu, and the test now asserts against the real catalogue that every approve/move write label of the three screens matches, while five read-only labels (among them «الاعتمادية») do not. The fix keeps the test's intent and does not weaken it: (1) My original reproduction, the full product e2e on the real stack (--workers=1), now passes the auditor test in both projects and both locale settings: unset 12.4 s en / 8.5 s ar; C.UTF-8 9.2 s / 7.1 s. Neither full run has a p3-prioritization-roadmap failure. (2) Adversarial mutants in the disposable clone: M1 shows the roadmap 'approve date' button to the auditor (canApprove = true) and M2 shows the 'move' button (canMove = true). Each makes the auditor test fail in chromium-en and chromium-ar at exactly the APPROVE_OR_MOVE assertion (spec line 530; 'Expected: 0, Received: 1'). On the restored build the spec passes 14/14. (3) My static probe of the matcher against every literal t() key of the three screens' 11 source files (en and ar) finds 0 button labels that the old matcher caught and the new one misses, except two that stay covered: dependencies.map.add is in the test's named-label assertion, and dependencies.form.save is that dialog's own submit. Every other old-only match is a non-button text (bodies, hints, column headers). A breadth limit that predates the fix is recorded as an observation in my record, not as part of this finding: neither assertion catches some write labels, such as decide, revoke, withdraw, archive or edit (Q2 of the probe). The old matcher did not catch them either.
